start.README.md:
# Skyline

A falling-blocks engine with tiny pieces. The engine is headless: a `Skyline` object, its legal moves and exact text for every reply. Everything is deterministic: pieces come from a generator that is specified exactly.

## Board and pieces

The board has 10 rows (row 0 at the top) and 6 columns (column 0 at the left). A cell is empty (`.`) or holds a locked block, remembered by the letter of the piece it came from.

Pieces are four small shapes:

| letter | cells as (row, column) offsets from the piece's origin |
|---|---|
| `I` | (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `L` | (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `D` | (0,0), (0,1) |
| `X` | (0,0) |

A piece is a list of offsets; the falling piece also has an *origin* cell `(row, col)` on the board, so the piece covers `(row + dr, col + dc)` for every offset. The offsets of the *current orientation* change when the piece rotates: a clockwise turn maps every offset `(dr, dc)` to `(dc, -dr)`, a counter-clockwise turn maps it to `(-dc, dr)` (the origin stays where it is).

### Randomness

`state` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Skyline(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2^32`. A *draw* sets `state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32` and returns `(state >> 24) mod 4`, the index into the letters `ILDX`. The game draws once at the start (that piece will be the first falling piece) and draws once more immediately to choose the next piece (it is *next*); afterwards every spawn takes `next` and then draws a new `next`. Nothing else draws.

### Spawning

A piece spawns in its base orientation with origin `(1, 3)` (row 1, column `W / 2` rounded down). If any of its cells is outside the board or on a locked block the game is over (the piece does not exist on the board, there are no legal moves and the game never changes again).

## Moves

Moves are exact strings: `left`, `right`, `cw`, `ccw`, `down`, `drop` (nothing else is accepted). `legalMoves()` lists the legal ones:

* `left`, `right`: legal when the piece fits one column to the left or right. Event `moved`.
* `cw`, `ccw`: rotate the piece. A rotation is legal only if the rotated piece fits with the origin where it is (there are no wall kicks). Event `rotated`.
* `down`: always legal while the game runs. If the piece fits one row lower it moves there, the score gains 1 point and the event is `fell`. Otherwise the piece *locks* (below).
* `drop`: always legal. The piece falls as far as it can, `n` rows (possibly 0); the score gains `n * 2` and the piece locks. Event `dropped <n> +<points>; ` followed by the lock event.

## Locking, clearing, scoring

When the piece locks its cells become locked blocks with the piece's letter. Then rows are cleared in *rounds*, `chain` starting at 1:

1. Collect the full rows (no empty cell). If there are none, stop.
2. With `k` full rows the score gains `10 * k * chain` points, `lines` grows by `k`. Remove the full rows (their cells become empty). The remaining rows move down to fill the gaps and empty rows appear at the top; the rows keep their order. 
3. `chain` grows by 1 and the next round starts.

(With row gravity compacting never makes a new full row, so a lock clears at most one round.)

Finally the next piece spawns. The lock event is `locked <letter>`, then for every round `; clear <k> x<chain> +<points>`, then `; spawn <letter of the new piece>` or `; game over`. Example: `locked L; clear 1 x1 +10; spawn I`.

## API (`Skyline.java`, default package)

```java
Skyline g = new Skyline(long seed);
List<String> g.legalMoves();   // legal moves in any order; empty when the game is over
String g.apply(String move);   // plays a legal move and returns the event; throws IllegalArgumentException (state unchanged) otherwise
String g.render();             // the board text (below)
int g.score();
boolean g.over();
```

### `render()`

10 board lines of 6 characters, then the footer. The footer line is `score <score> lines <lines>` followed by ` next <letter>` while the game runs or ` GAME OVER` when it is over. In the picture the falling piece is drawn with the *lower-case* letter of its piece (locked blocks keep their upper-case letters, empty cells are `.`); when the game is over there is no falling piece. Lines are joined by `\n`, there is no trailing newline.

```
......\n...x..\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n..III.\nscore 16 lines 0 next D
```

## Tests

`rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain` replays the scenario files in `test/data/` (`test/Adapter.java` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `test/TestMain.java`).

# Skyline

A falling-blocks engine with tiny pieces. The engine is headless: a `Skyline` object, its legal moves and exact text for every reply. Everything is deterministic: pieces come from a generator that is specified exactly.

## Board and pieces

The board has 10 rows (row 0 at the top) and 7 columns (column 0 at the left). A cell is empty (`.`) or holds a locked block, remembered by the letter of the piece it came from.

Pieces are four small shapes:

| letter | cells as (row, column) offsets from the piece's origin |
|---|---|
| `I` | (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `L` | (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `D` | (0,0), (0,1) |
| `X` | (0,0) |

A piece is a list of offsets; the falling piece also has an *origin* cell `(row, col)` on the board, so the piece covers `(row + dr, col + dc)` for every offset. The offsets of the *current orientation* change when the piece rotates: a clockwise turn maps every offset `(dr, dc)` to `(dc, -dr)`, a counter-clockwise turn maps it to `(-dc, dr)` (the origin stays where it is).

### Randomness

`state` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Skyline(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2^32`. A *draw* sets `state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32` and returns `(state >> 24) mod 4`, the index into the letters `ILDX`. The game draws once at the start (that piece will be the first falling piece) and draws once more immediately to choose the next piece (it is *next*); afterwards every spawn takes `next` and then draws a new `next`. Nothing else draws.

### Spawning

A piece spawns in its base orientation with origin `(1, 3)` (row 1, column `W / 2` rounded down). If any of its cells is outside the board or on a locked block the game is over (the piece does not exist on the board, there are no legal moves and the game never changes again).

## Moves

Moves are exact strings: `left`, `right`, `cw`, `ccw`, `down`, `drop` (nothing else is accepted). `legalMoves()` lists the legal ones:

* `left`, `right`: legal when the piece fits one column to the left or right. Event `moved`.
* `cw`, `ccw`: rotate the piece. A rotation is legal only if the rotated piece fits with the origin where it is (there are no wall kicks). Event `rotated`.
* `down`: always legal while the game runs. If the piece fits one row lower it moves there, the score gains 0 points and the event is `fell`. Otherwise the piece *locks* (below).
* `drop`: always legal. The piece falls as far as it can, `n` rows (possibly 0); the score gains `n * 1` and the piece locks. Event `dropped <n> +<points>; ` followed by the lock event.

## Locking, clearing, scoring

When the piece locks its cells become locked blocks with the piece's letter. Then rows are cleared in *rounds*, `chain` starting at 1:

1. Collect the full rows (no empty cell). If there are none, stop.
2. With `k` full rows the score gains `10 * k * chain` points, `lines` grows by `k`. Remove the full rows (their cells become empty). Every column is compacted downwards: the blocks of a column fall to the bottom of the board, keeping their order and their letters, until there are no gaps in the column (this also closes holes that existed before). 
3. `chain` grows by 1 and the next round starts.

(With column gravity a new full row can appear after the compaction, which is why chains exist.)

Finally the next piece spawns. The lock event is `locked <letter>`, then for every round `; clear <k> x<chain> +<points>`, then `; spawn <letter of the new piece>` or `; game over`. Example: `locked L; clear 1 x1 +10; spawn I`.

## API (`Skyline.java`, default package)

```java
Skyline g = new Skyline(long seed);
List<String> g.legalMoves();   // legal moves in any order; empty when the game is over
String g.apply(String move);   // plays a legal move and returns the event; throws IllegalArgumentException (state unchanged) otherwise
String g.render();             // the board text (below)
int g.score();
boolean g.over();
```

### `render()`

10 board lines of 7 characters, then the footer. The footer line is `score <score> lines <lines>` followed by ` next <letter>` while the game runs or ` GAME OVER` when it is over. In the picture the falling piece is drawn with the *lower-case* letter of its piece (locked blocks keep their upper-case letters, empty cells are `.`); when the game is over there is no falling piece. Lines are joined by `\n`, there is no trailing newline.

```
.......\n...x...\n.......\n.......\n.......\n.......\n.......\n.......\n.......\n..III..\nscore 8 lines 0 next D
```

`rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain` replays the scenario files in `test/data/` (`test/Adapter.java` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `test/TestMain.java`).

start.README.md:
# Skyline

A falling-blocks engine with tiny pieces. The engine is headless: a `Skyline` object, its legal moves and exact text for every reply. Everything is deterministic: pieces come from a generator that is specified exactly.

## Board and pieces

The board has 9 rows (row 0 at the top) and 6 columns (column 0 at the left). A cell is empty (`.`) or holds a locked block, remembered by the letter of the piece it came from.

Pieces are four small shapes:

| letter | cells as (row, column) offsets from the piece's origin |
|---|---|
| `I` | (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `L` | (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `D` | (0,0), (0,1) |
| `X` | (0,0) |

A piece is a list of offsets; the falling piece also has an *origin* cell `(row, col)` on the board, so the piece covers `(row + dr, col + dc)` for every offset. The offsets of the *current orientation* change when the piece rotates: a clockwise turn maps every offset `(dr, dc)` to `(dc, -dr)`, a counter-clockwise turn maps it to `(-dc, dr)` (the origin stays where it is).

### Randomness

`state` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Skyline(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2^32`. A *draw* sets `state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32` and returns `(state >> 24) mod 4`, the index into the letters `ILDX`. The game draws once at the start (that piece will be the first falling piece) and draws once more immediately to choose the next piece (it is *next*); afterwards every spawn takes `next` and then draws a new `next`. Nothing else draws.

### Spawning

A piece spawns in its base orientation with origin `(1, 3)` (row 1, column `W / 2` rounded down). If any of its cells is outside the board or on a locked block the game is over (the piece does not exist on the board, there are no legal moves and the game never changes again).

## Moves

Moves are exact strings: `left`, `right`, `cw`, `ccw`, `down`, `drop` (nothing else is accepted). `legalMoves()` lists the legal ones:

* `left`, `right`: legal when the piece fits one column to the left or right. Event `moved`.
* `cw`, `ccw`: rotate the piece. If the rotated piece does not fit, the rotation is retried with the origin moved one column left (`col - 1`) and then one column right (`col + 1`); the first position that fits is used and the origin moves with it. If none fits the rotation is illegal. Event `rotated`.
* `down`: always legal while the game runs. If the piece fits one row lower it moves there, the score gains 1 point and the event is `fell`. Otherwise the piece *locks* (below).
* `drop`: always legal. The piece falls as far as it can, `n` rows (possibly 0); the score gains `n * 2` and the piece locks. Event `dropped <n> +<points>; ` followed by the lock event.

## Locking, clearing, scoring

When the piece locks its cells become locked blocks with the piece's letter. Then rows are cleared in *rounds*, `chain` starting at 1:

1. Collect the full rows (no empty cell). If there are none, stop.
2. With `k` full rows the score gains `10 * k * chain` points, `lines` grows by `k`. Remove the full rows (their cells become empty). The remaining rows move down to fill the gaps and empty rows appear at the top; the rows keep their order. 
3. `chain` grows by 1 and the next round starts.

(With row gravity compacting never makes a new full row, so a lock clears at most one round.)

Finally the next piece spawns. The lock event is `locked <letter>`, then for every round `; clear <k> x<chain> +<points>`, then `; spawn <letter of the new piece>` or `; game over`. Example: `locked L; clear 1 x1 +10; spawn I`.

## API (`Skyline.java`, default package)

```java
Skyline g = new Skyline(long seed);
List<String> g.legalMoves();   // legal moves in any order; empty when the game is over
String g.apply(String move);   // plays a legal move and returns the event; throws IllegalArgumentException (state unchanged) otherwise
String g.render();             // the board text (below)
int g.score();
boolean g.over();
```

### `render()`

9 board lines of 6 characters, then the footer. The footer line is `score <score> lines <lines>` followed by ` next <letter>` while the game runs or ` GAME OVER` when it is over. In the picture the falling piece is drawn with the *lower-case* letter of its piece (locked blocks keep their upper-case letters, empty cells are `.`); when the game is over there is no falling piece. Lines are joined by `\n`, there is no trailing newline.

```
......\n...x..\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n..III.\nscore 14 lines 0 next D
```

## Tests

`rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain` replays the scenario files in `test/data/` (`test/Adapter.java` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `test/TestMain.java`).

start.README.md:
# Skyline

A falling-blocks engine with tiny pieces. The engine is headless: a `Skyline` object, its legal moves and exact text for every reply. Everything is deterministic: pieces come from a generator that is specified exactly.

## Board and pieces

The board has 11 rows (row 0 at the top) and 8 columns (column 0 at the left). A cell is empty (`.`) or holds a locked block, remembered by the letter of the piece it came from.

Pieces are four small shapes:

| letter | cells as (row, column) offsets from the piece's origin |
|---|---|
| `I` | (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `L` | (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `D` | (0,0), (0,1) |
| `X` | (0,0) |

A piece is a list of offsets; the falling piece also has an *origin* cell `(row, col)` on the board, so the piece covers `(row + dr, col + dc)` for every offset. The offsets of the *current orientation* change when the piece rotates: a clockwise turn maps every offset `(dr, dc)` to `(dc, -dr)`, a counter-clockwise turn maps it to `(-dc, dr)` (the origin stays where it is).

### Randomness

`state` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Skyline(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2^32`. A *draw* sets `state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32` and returns `(state >> 24) mod 4`, the index into the letters `ILDX`. The game draws once at the start (that piece will be the first falling piece) and draws once more immediately to choose the next piece (it is *next*); afterwards every spawn takes `next` and then draws a new `next`. Nothing else draws.

### Spawning

A piece spawns in its base orientation with origin `(1, 4)` (row 1, column `W / 2` rounded down). If any of its cells is outside the board or on a locked block the game is over (the piece does not exist on the board, there are no legal moves and the game never changes again).

## Moves

Moves are exact strings: `left`, `right`, `cw`, `ccw`, `down`, `drop` (nothing else is accepted). `legalMoves()` lists the legal ones:

* `left`, `right`: legal when the piece fits one column to the left or right. Event `moved`.
* `cw`, `ccw`: rotate the piece. If the rotated piece does not fit, the rotation is retried with the origin moved one column left (`col - 1`) and then one column right (`col + 1`); the first position that fits is used and the origin moves with it. If none fits the rotation is illegal. Event `rotated`.
* `down`: always legal while the game runs. If the piece fits one row lower it moves there, the score gains 1 point and the event is `fell`. Otherwise the piece *locks* (below).
* `drop`: always legal. The piece falls as far as it can, `n` rows (possibly 0); the score gains `n * 2` and the piece locks. Event `dropped <n> +<points>; ` followed by the lock event.

## Locking, clearing, scoring

When the piece locks its cells become locked blocks with the piece's letter. Then rows are cleared in *rounds*, `chain` starting at 1:

1. Collect the full rows (no empty cell). If there are none, stop.
2. With `k` full rows the score gains `15 * k * chain` points, `lines` grows by `k`. Remove the full rows (their cells become empty). Every column is compacted downwards: the blocks of a column fall to the bottom of the board, keeping their order and their letters, until there are no gaps in the column (this also closes holes that existed before). 
3. `chain` grows by 1 and the next round starts.

(With column gravity a new full row can appear after the compaction, which is why chains exist.)

Finally the next piece spawns. The lock event is `locked <letter>`, then for every round `; clear <k> x<chain> +<points>`, then `; spawn <letter of the new piece>` or `; game over`. Example: `locked L; clear 1 x1 +10; spawn I`.

## API (`Skyline.java`, default package)

```java
Skyline g = new Skyline(long seed);
List<String> g.legalMoves();   // legal moves in any order; empty when the game is over
String g.apply(String move);   // plays a legal move and returns the event; throws IllegalArgumentException (state unchanged) otherwise
String g.render();             // the board text (below)
int g.score();
boolean g.over();
```

### `render()`

11 board lines of 8 characters, then the footer. The footer line is `score <score> lines <lines>` followed by ` next <letter>` while the game runs or ` GAME OVER` when it is over. In the picture the falling piece is drawn with the *lower-case* letter of its piece (locked blocks keep their upper-case letters, empty cells are `.`); when the game is over there is no falling piece. Lines are joined by `\n`, there is no trailing newline.

```
........\n....x...\n........\n........\n........\n........\n........\n........\n........\n........\n...III..\nscore 18 lines 0 next D
```

## Tests

`rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain` replays the scenario files in `test/data/` (`test/Adapter.java` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `test/TestMain.java`).

start.README.md:
# Skyline

A falling-blocks engine with tiny pieces. The engine is headless: a `Skyline` object, its legal moves and exact text for every reply. Everything is deterministic: pieces come from a generator that is specified exactly.

## Board and pieces

The board has 9 rows (row 0 at the top) and 5 columns (column 0 at the left). A cell is empty (`.`) or holds a locked block, remembered by the letter of the piece it came from.

Pieces are four small shapes:

| letter | cells as (row, column) offsets from the piece's origin |
|---|---|
| `I` | (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `L` | (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `D` | (0,0), (0,1) |
| `X` | (0,0) |

A piece is a list of offsets; the falling piece also has an *origin* cell `(row, col)` on the board, so the piece covers `(row + dr, col + dc)` for every offset. The offsets of the *current orientation* change when the piece rotates: a clockwise turn maps every offset `(dr, dc)` to `(dc, -dr)`, a counter-clockwise turn maps it to `(-dc, dr)` (the origin stays where it is).

### Randomness

`state` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Skyline(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2^32`. A *draw* sets `state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32` and returns `(state >> 24) mod 4`, the index into the letters `ILDX`. The game draws once at the start (that piece will be the first falling piece) and draws once more immediately to choose the next piece (it is *next*); afterwards every spawn takes `next` and then draws a new `next`. Nothing else draws.

### Spawning

A piece spawns in its base orientation with origin `(1, 2)` (row 1, column `W / 2` rounded down). If any of its cells is outside the board or on a locked block the game is over (the piece does not exist on the board, there are no legal moves and the game never changes again).

## Moves

Moves are exact strings: `left`, `right`, `cw`, `ccw`, `down`, `drop` (nothing else is accepted). `legalMoves()` lists the legal ones:

* `left`, `right`: legal when the piece fits one column to the left or right. Event `moved`.
* `cw`, `ccw`: rotate the piece. A rotation is legal only if the rotated piece fits with the origin where it is (there are no wall kicks). Event `rotated`.
* `down`: always legal while the game runs. If the piece fits one row lower it moves there, the score gains 1 point and the event is `fell`. Otherwise the piece *locks* (below).
* `drop`: always legal. The piece falls as far as it can, `n` rows (possibly 0); the score gains `n * 2` and the piece locks. Event `dropped <n> +<points>; ` followed by the lock event.

## Locking, clearing, scoring

When the piece locks its cells become locked blocks with the piece's letter. Then rows are cleared in *rounds*, `chain` starting at 1:

1. Collect the full rows (no empty cell). If there are none, stop.
2. With `k` full rows the score gains `20 * k * chain` points, `lines` grows by `k`. Remove the full rows (their cells become empty). Every column is compacted downwards: the blocks of a column fall to the bottom of the board, keeping their order and their letters, until there are no gaps in the column (this also closes holes that existed before). 
3. `chain` grows by 1 and the next round starts.

(With column gravity a new full row can appear after the compaction, which is why chains exist.)

Finally the next piece spawns. The lock event is `locked <letter>`, then for every round `; clear <k> x<chain> +<points>`, then `; spawn <letter of the new piece>` or `; game over`. Example: `locked L; clear 1 x1 +10; spawn I`.

## API (`Skyline.java`, default package)

```java
Skyline g = new Skyline(long seed);
List<String> g.legalMoves();   // legal moves in any order; empty when the game is over
String g.apply(String move);   // plays a legal move and returns the event; throws IllegalArgumentException (state unchanged) otherwise
String g.render();             // the board text (below)
int g.score();
boolean g.over();
```

### `render()`

9 board lines of 5 characters, then the footer. The footer line is `score <score> lines <lines>` followed by ` next <letter>` while the game runs or ` GAME OVER` when it is over. In the picture the falling piece is drawn with the *lower-case* letter of its piece (locked blocks keep their upper-case letters, empty cells are `.`); when the game is over there is no falling piece. Lines are joined by `\n`, there is no trailing newline.

```
.....\n..x..\n.....\n.....\n.....\n.....\n.....\n.....\n.III.\nscore 14 lines 0 next D
```

## Tests

`rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain` replays the scenario files in `test/data/` (`test/Adapter.java` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `test/TestMain.java`).

start.README.md:
# Skyline

A falling-blocks engine with tiny pieces. The engine is headless: a `Skyline` object, its legal moves and exact text for every reply. Everything is deterministic: pieces come from a generator that is specified exactly.

## Board and pieces

The board has 12 rows (row 0 at the top) and 6 columns (column 0 at the left). A cell is empty (`.`) or holds a locked block, remembered by the letter of the piece it came from.

Pieces are four small shapes:

| letter | cells as (row, column) offsets from the piece's origin |
|---|---|
| `I` | (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `L` | (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1) |
| `D` | (0,0), (0,1) |
| `X` | (0,0) |

A piece is a list of offsets; the falling piece also has an *origin* cell `(row, col)` on the board, so the piece covers `(row + dr, col + dc)` for every offset. The offsets of the *current orientation* change when the piece rotates: a clockwise turn maps every offset `(dr, dc)` to `(dc, -dr)`, a counter-clockwise turn maps it to `(-dc, dr)` (the origin stays where it is).

### Randomness

`state` is an unsigned 32-bit integer. `Skyline(seed)` starts with `state = seed mod 2^32`. A *draw* sets `state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32` and returns `(state >> 24) mod 4`, the index into the letters `ILDX`. The game draws once at the start (that piece will be the first falling piece) and draws once more immediately to choose the next piece (it is *next*); afterwards every spawn takes `next` and then draws a new `next`. Nothing else draws.

### Spawning

A piece spawns in its base orientation with origin `(1, 3)` (row 1, column `W / 2` rounded down). If any of its cells is outside the board or on a locked block the game is over (the piece does not exist on the board, there are no legal moves and the game never changes again).

## Moves

Moves are exact strings: `left`, `right`, `cw`, `ccw`, `down`, `drop` (nothing else is accepted). `legalMoves()` lists the legal ones:

* `left`, `right`: legal when the piece fits one column to the left or right. Event `moved`.
* `cw`, `ccw`: rotate the piece. If the rotated piece does not fit, the rotation is retried with the origin moved one column left (`col - 1`) and then one column right (`col + 1`); the first position that fits is used and the origin moves with it. If none fits the rotation is illegal. Event `rotated`.
* `down`: always legal while the game runs. If the piece fits one row lower it moves there, the score gains 2 points and the event is `fell`. Otherwise the piece *locks* (below).
* `drop`: always legal. The piece falls as far as it can, `n` rows (possibly 0); the score gains `n * 3` and the piece locks. Event `dropped <n> +<points>; ` followed by the lock event.

## Locking, clearing, scoring

When the piece locks its cells become locked blocks with the piece's letter. Then rows are cleared in *rounds*, `chain` starting at 1:

1. Collect the full rows (no empty cell). If there are none, stop.
2. With `k` full rows the score gains `15 * k * chain` points, `lines` grows by `k`. Remove the full rows (their cells become empty). The remaining rows move down to fill the gaps and empty rows appear at the top; the rows keep their order. 
3. `chain` grows by 1 and the next round starts.

(With row gravity compacting never makes a new full row, so a lock clears at most one round.)

Finally the next piece spawns. The lock event is `locked <letter>`, then for every round `; clear <k> x<chain> +<points>`, then `; spawn <letter of the new piece>` or `; game over`. Example: `locked L; clear 1 x1 +10; spawn I`.

## API (`Skyline.java`, default package)

```java
Skyline g = new Skyline(long seed);
List<String> g.legalMoves();   // legal moves in any order; empty when the game is over
String g.apply(String move);   // plays a legal move and returns the event; throws IllegalArgumentException (state unchanged) otherwise
String g.render();             // the board text (below)
int g.score();
boolean g.over();
```

### `render()`

12 board lines of 6 characters, then the footer. The footer line is `score <score> lines <lines>` followed by ` next <letter>` while the game runs or ` GAME OVER` when it is over. In the picture the falling piece is drawn with the *lower-case* letter of its piece (locked blocks keep their upper-case letters, empty cells are `.`); when the game is over there is no falling piece. Lines are joined by `\n`, there is no trailing newline.

```
......\n...x..\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n......\n..III.\nscore 30 lines 0 next D
```

## Tests

`rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain` replays the scenario files in `test/data/` (`test/Adapter.java` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `test/TestMain.java`).
